programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha na planntraisean 's na lusan aig Mamaidh ri cleòcadh san teas ach, gu fortanach, tha deagh bheachd aig Meanbh airson Mamaidh a chuideachadh len uisgeachadh. Mother’s plants and flowers are wilting in the heat but fortunately, Tiny has a brilliant idea to help Mother out with watering.

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Tha na Losgannan a’ cruthachadh còmhlan-ciùil roc le maracas, drumaichean agus sacsafòn! After finding some pasta, the Froglets create a rock band with maracas, drum and saxophone!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Chan eil sgeul air Mossy 's tha Oona a sìor fhàs iomagaineach mu cà dh'fhaodadh a caraid a bhith. Ann a bhith ga lorg, tha i faighinn cuideachadh ris nach robh i an dùil - bho Flynne an sionnach 'seòlta'! Mossy is missing and Oona becomes increasingly worried about where her friend could be. In trying to find him, she is offered help from a very unlikely source - Flynne the 'sly' fox!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha faiche nam buthaidean ga glanadh 's tha Oona 's Baba airsona bhith nan cuideachadh... a cur romhpa stuth bog a' lorg a ni leabaidh mhath ùr, tha iad a' tighinn an aghaidh ioma cnap-starra! The puffin burrow is undergoing a major clean-out and both Oona and Baba desperately want to help out. They decide to collect soft things to make a new bed, leading to an unexpected adventure.

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha caraidean Pheicein ag innse dha mun t-sanas ùr aig “Silidh Milis Steigeach”, ma ghlèidheas tu ochd bileagan bho na mullaich, gheibh thu paidhir spèileachain. ’S e an trioblaid, gu bheil blas grot far “Silidh Milis Steigeach”. Petit finds out if you collect eight Really Tasty Candy lids you get a free pair of roller skates! The only catch is Really Tasty Candy tastes really, really, bad...

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Thig air sgrìob eile cuide ri na h-Abadas 's iad ri tuilleadh spors 's ploigh aba-doo-bee-dee fhad 's a tha iad air toir an fhacal 'glainne-meudachaidh'. Ela is very tired today, but is she too exhausted to play the word game? Join the Abadas as one of them heads off for another aba-doo-be-dee island adventure to find today's word, 'magnifying glass'.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachd do chlann òga. Tha Ruairidh Gray a’ leughadh An Dannsa Mòr. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh agus a dhealbhachadh le Aoife Greenham, agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. Ruairidh Gray reads An Dannsa Mòr, written and illustrated by Aoife Greenham and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royals Next Door
programme.desc: Nuair a tha an clas a' faighinn cothrom turas campachaidh bhith aca, tha Stella, ‘s i na h-eòlaiche na beachd fhèin, airson 's gun tèid i fhèin, Mia is Freya, 'son practas sa ghàrradh an toiseach – ach saoil am bi seo soirbheachail? When the class gets the chance to go on a camping trip, Stella, who’s an expert in her own opinion, wants to practise in the garden with Mia and Freya - but will this be successful?

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royals Next Door
programme.desc: Ged a tha Stella cleachdte ri bhith bruidhinn air beulaibh dhaoine, ‘s e rud eile a th’ ann a h-òraid a sgrìobhadh dhi fhèin cuideachd. Tha i fortanach gu bheil deagh charaidean aice, ge-tà! Although Stella is used to public speaking, it’s another thing altogether to have to write her own speech, too. She’s fortunate to have good friends though.

programme.title: Clann Na Cruinne
programme.desc: Is caomh le Tòmas a bhith cur seachad ùine le crodh. Tha e mar gu bheil iad dha thuigsinn. Nuair a tha droch là aige san sgoil, thig iad thuige is bruidhnidh e riutha. Tha e airson a bhith na bhuachaille nuair a dh’fhàsas e mòr. Tòmas loves to spend time with cows - they seem to understand him. When he’s had a bad day at school, they come to him and he talks to them. He wants to be a herdsman when he grows up.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Nuair nach eil sgeul air Belle, tha Sebastian draghail oir 's e seo an treas trup an t-seachdain seo – 's tha e 'g ionndrainn an caidreadh maidne aca. Ach dè tha ag adhbharachadh seo? When Belle is nowhere to be seen, Sebastian is anxious as this is the third time this week, and he misses their morning hugs. But what could be causing this?

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha Tbh ùr aig an tuathanach is abair gu bheil e toilichte. The farmer is very excited about his new TV.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Brunch le Abigail
programme.desc: Tha Abigail a’ dèanamh Rola Bracaist, fìor rionnag a’ bhìdh agus a’ bhracaist as fheàrr a bhios agad an-diugh. Bidh do chàirdean ’s do charaidean air an dòigh glan leis a’ rola bhracaist seo a tha uabhasach fhèin blasta, agus a shàsaicheas miann sam bith. Abigail makes a breakfast roll, a real show-stopper among family and friends. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Machair
programme.desc: Drama Gàidhlig stèidhichte ann an Leòdhas. Gaelic soap based on the Isle of Lewis.

programme.title: Mach à Seo!
programme.desc: Ramsay MacMahon heads off on a trip through Dalbeattie and Lockerbie. He learns about the area’s granite industry, samples a local delicacy and becomes a farmer for the afternoon.

programme.title: An Clo Mor
programme.desc: It’s the day of Sìleas and Seumas’s vow renewal. But while Sìleas is excited, Seumas seems preoccupied. His son Dòmhnall also has a lot on his mind. Will he be able to reconcile himself to the fact that Ivor is going to be a father? Meanwhile Seumas’s other son Shonnie is missing. So, will Sìleas and Seumas’s ceremony go ahead as planned? ‘S e latha mòr ùrachadh nam bòidean a th’ ann do Sheumas is do Shìleas. Fhad ‘s a Sìleas air bhioran, tha rudeigin a’ cur dragh air Seumas. Tha tòrr cuideachd aig a mhac, Dòmhnall, air aire. An tèid aige air gabhail ris gu bheil Ivor gu bhith na athair? Tha Shonnie, am mac eile aig Seumas, air a dhol a dhìth. An tèid an latha mòr aig Sìleas is Seumas mar bu chòir san earrann mu dheireadh dhen t-sreath? In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Rocaidean gu Leor (Rockets Galore)
programme.desc: Tha fanas a’ toirt buaidh mhòr air ar beatha laitheil, gu h-àraid a thaobh teicneolas. Tha luach na builleanan de notaicean an gnìomhachas an fhanais agus tha Alba air aon de na dùthchanan a thana theis-mheadhain. Thigibh còmhla ri Mairi Rodgers ’s i a coinneachadh ri daoine a tha a’dèanamh rocaidean mar chur-seachad, oileanaich a tha airson obair fhaighinn sa ghniomhachais agus cuid de na companaidhean a tha a’ sas ann. Bidh I cuideachd a tadhal air coimhearnsnachdan far a bheil feadhainn gu mòr ag iarraidh port-fanais san nabachd aca agus feadhainn eile gu tur na aghaidh. Space massively impacts our daily lives, especially in the technology that we use. The industry is worth billions of pounds and Scotland is one of the countries at the heart of that industry. Join Mairi Rodgers as she meets amateur rocketeers, students who hope to work in the industry and some of the companies involved. She also visits communities where spaceports are planned - with some warmly embracing the hubs and others determined to block them.

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc: Mary Ann Kennedy and Lucy Cooke drum up a foraged feast with friends at the Wildluing Observatory in Argyll.

programme.title: An Cruinne Caochlaideach/Dynamic Planet
programme.desc: As the ice drastically melts, we see how science, nature and tradition can prepare us for the future.

programme.title: Belladrum
programme.desc: Tha Fiona NicChoinnich is Niall Iain Dòmhnallach a’ cur fàilt’ oirbh chun a’ chiad latha aig Belladrum 2025. Anns a’ phrògram seo, bidh an seinneadair cliùiteach Paul Heaton, a bha soirbheachail mar phrìomh sheinneadair dhen bhuidheann indie rock bho na 80an, The Housemartins. Cuide ri Paul air Àrd-Ùrlar Hot House tha Rianne Downey aige air aoigheachd, airson an oidhche a thoirt gu ceann. Fiona MacKenzie and Niall Iain Macdonald welcome you to the first day at Belladrum 2025. This programme features renowned singer Paul Heaton, who was successful as the lead singer of 80s indie rock group The Housemartins. Joining Paul on the Hot House Stage to bring the night to a close is special guest Rianne Downey.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Double Cross: The True Story of the D-Day Spies
programme.desc: The story of D-Day has been told from the point of view of the soldiers who fought in it, the tacticians who planned it and the generals who led it. But that epic event in world history has never been told before through the perspective of the strange handful of spies who made it possible. D-Day was a great victory of arms, a tactical coup, and a moral crusade. But it was also a triumph for espionage, deceit, and thinking of the most twisted sort. Following on from his hugely successful BBC Two documentaries, Operation Mincemeat and Double Agent: The Eddie Chapman Story (Agent Zigzag), writer and presenter Ben Macintyre returns to the small screen to bring to life his third best-selling book - Double Cross The True Story of the D-Day Spies. Macintyre reveals the gripping true story of five of the double agents who helped to make D-Day such a success.

programme.title: imagine...
programme.desc: At the age of 91, Mel Brooks is unstoppable, with his musical Young Frankenstein opening to great critical acclaim in London in late 2017. Alan Yentob visits Mel at home in Hollywood, at work and at play. With the aid of BBC archive stretching back decades, together they embark on an unpredictable, irresistible journey through the city of stars, meeting the legendary Carl Reiner along the way. The driver is Mel Brooks - you have been warned!

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: Following the sentencing of 13 people for violent disorder during protests in Southampton, attention has turned to the role of content creators who film demonstrations and public disorder. The judge cited the usefulness of footage filmed by so-called 'citizen journalists'. Siddharth Venkataramakrishnan of the Institute for Strategic Dialogue and content creator Wesley Winter give their perspective on the issue. The BBC has begun setting out changes as part of plans to deliver significant savings across the organisation. The measures include the closure of several programmes across radio and current affairs output, alongside wider reductions in staffing. Jonathan Munro, global director of BBC News, outlines the changes. Norma Percy has spent years getting to the heart of some of the biggest moments in recent history. Her documentaries have been celebrated for talking directly to the people who made the decisions. As the BBC airs her latest film - about Brexit - she reflects on her storied career and the future of documentary-making.

programme.title: Fraud Squad
programme.desc: The Environment Agency gets called in when a waste site flouts the rules and local residents start complaining. The facility is supposed to be a plastics recycling plant, but lorry loads of illegal waste are being delivered on a regular basis. Investigators decide to take a look, and what they find rings alarm bells – piles and piles of waste covering the site. Not only is it way beyond what’s permitted to be on a plastics recycling site, but more worryingly, it’s not being stored properly and there’s a genuine risk of it catching fire as a result. The Environment Agency takes swift action. In a second case, Trading Standards are called in after a spate of fake Sky TV remote controls flood the local market. As officers start to investigate, they unearth a massive operation in fake goods being sold on online auction sites. As well as remote controls, the seller has electrical items and cosmetics up for sale, all pretending to be from well-known brands. It’s putting consumers at risk and running up a massive bill in unpaid tax – money which should be in the public purse.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A 22-year-old developer tackles a very ambitious project in Merseyside, Martel is optimistic about the prospects of a house in County Durham, and Martin falls for the charms of a characterful bungalow in Dorset.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: They have been raising smiles for centuries, and in this episode, Eric Knowles learns about a unique clowning tradition. No two clowns should look alike, which is why their faces are copyrighted – on painted eggs! Professional clown Mattie Faint prompts a chuckle or two from Eric when he explains this egg-centric custom. Topping the bill on this show are two teams of antiques hunters, browsing hundreds of stalls at a huge fair with experts Nick Hall and Izzie Balmer. With 60 minutes on the clock, grandmother and granddaughter Karen and Amelia stew over an art deco tea set, while the reds, friends Stuart and Martin, reckon they spy a profit with a pair of mother of pearl opera glasses. Selling their items is auctioneer Charles Hanson in nearby Derbyshire. Which team is his money on?

programme.desc: Jules Hudson helps a couple to come back to Blighty after 16 years down under. Their £450,000 budget might not stretch quite as far in Lancashire as it did in Oz, but Jules still has a great selection of properties that are reminiscent of the home they have left behind. He also manages to squeeze in a visit to a nature reserve, created at a quarry used to build the UK’s first motorway.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie Dimmock returns to Hampshire to see one of the gardens she designed with the Rich Brothers. Sheena and Jim had wanted a relaxed, seaside-inspired space for entertaining, and Charlie is delighted to see how they have truly made it their own. Charlie also heads back to Coventry to revisit the fun-filled activity garden she created for Louise and her children, now transformed into a mature haven brimming with shrubs and flowers. Finally, Charlie catches up with Debs and Nige in Oldham, whose dream of a mid-century–inspired garden has blossomed into a stylish retreat perfect for family and friends.

programme.title: Morning Live
programme.desc: Join Gethin Jones, Helen Skelton, Michelle Ackerley and the team for conversation, advice and tips to make your day that little bit easier.

programme.title: Fraud Squad
programme.desc: The Environment Agency gets called in when a waste site flouts the rules and local residents start complaining. The facility is supposed to be a plastics recycling plant, but lorry loads of illegal waste are being delivered on a regular basis. Investigators decide to take a look, and what they find rings alarm bells – piles and piles of waste covering the site. Not only is it way beyond what’s permitted to be on a plastics recycling site, but more worryingly, it’s not being stored properly and there’s a genuine risk of it catching fire as a result. The Environment Agency takes swift action. In a second case, Trading Standards are called in after a spate of fake Sky TV remote controls flood the local market. As officers start to investigate, they unearth a massive operation in fake goods being sold on online auction sites. As well as remote controls, the seller has electrical items and cosmetics up for sale, all pretending to be from well-known brands. It’s putting consumers at risk and running up a massive bill in unpaid tax – money which should be in the public purse.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A 22-year-old developer tackles a very ambitious project in Merseyside, Martel is optimistic about the prospects of a house in County Durham, and Martin falls for the charms of a characterful bungalow in Dorset.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: They have been raising smiles for centuries, and in this episode, Eric Knowles learns about a unique clowning tradition. No two clowns should look alike, which is why their faces are copyrighted – on painted eggs! Professional clown Mattie Faint prompts a chuckle or two from Eric when he explains this egg-centric custom. Topping the bill on this show are two teams of antiques hunters, browsing hundreds of stalls at a huge fair with experts Nick Hall and Izzie Balmer. With 60 minutes on the clock, grandmother and granddaughter Karen and Amelia stew over an art deco tea set, while the reds, friends Stuart and Martin, reckon they spy a profit with a pair of mother of pearl opera glasses. Selling their items is auctioneer Charles Hanson in nearby Derbyshire. Which team is his money on?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Jules Hudson helps a couple to come back to Blighty after 16 years down under. Their £450,000 budget might not stretch quite as far in Lancashire as it did in Oz, but Jules still has a great selection of properties that are reminiscent of the home they have left behind. He also manages to squeeze in a visit to a nature reserve, created at a quarry used to build the UK’s first motorway.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie Dimmock returns to Hampshire to see one of the gardens she designed with the Rich Brothers. Sheena and Jim had wanted a relaxed, seaside-inspired space for entertaining, and Charlie is delighted to see how they have truly made it their own. Charlie also heads back to Coventry to revisit the fun-filled activity garden she created for Louise and her children, now transformed into a mature haven brimming with shrubs and flowers. Finally, Charlie catches up with Debs and Nige in Oldham, whose dream of a mid-century–inspired garden has blossomed into a stylish retreat perfect for family and friends.

programme.title: Fraud Squad
programme.desc: The Environment Agency gets called in when a waste site flouts the rules and local residents start complaining. The facility is supposed to be a plastics recycling plant, but lorry loads of illegal waste are being delivered on a regular basis. Investigators decide to take a look, and what they find rings alarm bells – piles and piles of waste covering the site. Not only is it way beyond what’s permitted to be on a plastics recycling site, but more worryingly, it’s not being stored properly and there’s a genuine risk of it catching fire as a result. The Environment Agency takes swift action. In a second case, Trading Standards are called in after a spate of fake Sky TV remote controls flood the local market. As officers start to investigate, they unearth a massive operation in fake goods being sold on online auction sites. As well as remote controls, the seller has electrical items and cosmetics up for sale, all pretending to be from well-known brands. It’s putting consumers at risk and running up a massive bill in unpaid tax – money which should be in the public purse.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A 22-year-old developer tackles a very ambitious project in Merseyside, Martel is optimistic about the prospects of a house in County Durham, and Martin falls for the charms of a characterful bungalow in Dorset.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: They have been raising smiles for centuries, and in this episode, Eric Knowles learns about a unique clowning tradition. No two clowns should look alike, which is why their faces are copyrighted – on painted eggs! Professional clown Mattie Faint prompts a chuckle or two from Eric when he explains this egg-centric custom. Topping the bill on this show are two teams of antiques hunters, browsing hundreds of stalls at a huge fair with experts Nick Hall and Izzie Balmer. With 60 minutes on the clock, grandmother and granddaughter Karen and Amelia stew over an art deco tea set, while the reds, friends Stuart and Martin, reckon they spy a profit with a pair of mother of pearl opera glasses. Selling their items is auctioneer Charles Hanson in nearby Derbyshire. Which team is his money on?

programme.title: Fraud Squad
programme.desc: The Environment Agency gets called in when a waste site flouts the rules and local residents start complaining. Investigators decide to take a look, and what they find rings alarm bells – piles and piles of waste covering the site. programme.title: King Richard

programme.title: Fraud Squad
programme.desc: The Environment Agency gets called in when a waste site flouts the rules and local residents start complaining. The facility is supposed to be a plastics recycling plant, but lorry loads of illegal waste are being delivered on a regular basis. Investigators decide to take a look, and what they find rings alarm bells – piles and piles of waste covering the site. Not only is it way beyond what’s permitted to be on a plastics recycling site, but more worryingly, it’s not being stored properly and there’s a genuine risk of it catching fire as a result. The Environment Agency takes swift action. In a second case, Trading Standards are called in after a spate of fake Sky TV remote controls flood the local market. As officers start to investigate, they unearth a massive operation in fake goods being sold on online auction sites. As well as remote controls, the seller has electrical items and cosmetics up for sale, all pretending to be from well-known brands. It’s putting consumers at risk and running up a massive bill in unpaid tax – money which should be in the public purse.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A 22-year-old developer tackles a very ambitious project in Merseyside, Martel is optimistic about the prospects of a house in County Durham, and Martin falls for the charms of a characterful bungalow in Dorset.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: They have been raising smiles for centuries, and in this episode, Eric Knowles learns about a unique clowning tradition. No two clowns should look alike, which is why their faces are copyrighted – on painted eggs! Professional clown Mattie Faint prompts a chuckle or two from Eric when he explains this egg-centric custom. Topping the bill on this show are two teams of antiques hunters, browsing hundreds of stalls at a huge fair with experts Nick Hall and Izzie Balmer. With 60 minutes on the clock, grandmother and granddaughter Karen and Amelia stew over an art deco tea set, while the reds, friends Stuart and Martin, reckon they spy a profit with a pair of mother of pearl opera glasses. Selling their items is auctioneer Charles Hanson in nearby Derbyshire. Which team is his money on?

programme.title: Fraud Squad

Their £450,000 budget might not stretch quite as far in Lancashire as it did in Oz, but Jules still has a great selection of properties that are reminiscent of the home they have left behind. He also manages to squeeze in a visit to a nature reserve, created at a quarry used to build the UK’s first motorway.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie Dimmock returns to Hampshire to see one of the gardens she designed with the Rich Brothers. Sheena and Jim had wanted a relaxed, seaside-inspired space for entertaining, and Charlie is delighted to see how they have truly made it their own. Charlie also heads back to Coventry to revisit the fun-filled activity garden she created for Louise and her children, now transformed into a mature haven brimming with shrubs and flowers. Finally, Charlie catches up with Debs and Nige in Oldham, whose dream of a mid-century–inspired garden has blossomed into a stylish retreat perfect for family and friends.

programme.title: Fraud Squad
programme.desc: The Environment Agency gets called in when a waste site flouts the rules and local residents start complaining. The facility is supposed to be a plastics recycling plant, but lorry loads of illegal waste are being delivered on a regular basis. Investigators decide to take a look, and what they find rings alarm bells – piles and piles of waste covering the site. Not only is it way beyond what’s permitted to be on a plastics recycling site, but more worryingly, it’s not being stored properly and there’s a genuine risk of it catching fire as a result. The Environment Agency takes swift action. In a second case, Trading Standards are called in after a spate of fake Sky TV remote controls flood the local market. As officers start to investigate, they unearth a massive operation in fake goods being sold on online auction sites. As well as remote controls, the seller has electrical items and cosmetics up for sale, all pretending to be from well-known brands. It’s putting consumers at risk and running up a massive bill in unpaid tax – money which should be in the public purse.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A 22-year-old developer tackles a very ambitious project in Merseyside, Martel is optimistic about the prospects of a house in County Durham, and Martin falls for the charms of a characterful bungalow in Dorset.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: They have been raising smiles for centuries, and in this episode, Eric Knowles learns about a unique clowning tradition. No two clowns should look alike, which is why their faces are copyrighted – on painted eggs! Professional clown Mattie Faint prompts a chuckle or two from Eric when he explains this egg-centric custom. Topping the bill on this show are two teams of antiques hunters, browsing hundreds of stalls at a huge fair with experts Nick Hall and Izzie Balmer. With 60 minutes on the clock, grandmother and granddaughter Karen and Amelia stew over an art deco tea set, while the reds, friends Stuart and Martin, reckon they spy a profit with a pair of mother of pearl opera glasses. Selling their items is auctioneer Charles Hanson in nearby Derbyshire. Which team is his money on?

programme.title: Fraud Squad
programme.desc: The Environment Agency gets called in when a waste site flouts the rules and local residents start complaining. Investigators decide to take a look, and what they find rings alarm bells – piles and piles of waste covering the site. programme.title: My Epic Camel Adventure with Gordon Buchanan
programme.desc: Gordon Buchanan takes an epic journey across the Gobi Desert on one of the world’s most iconic, yet least understood, animals – camels. Starting in the west of Mongolia, Gordeon crosses blistering sand dunes, endless rocky plains and the treacherous Bumbat Mountain, with only his camels for company. If he is to succeed, he must befriend the camels, learn as much as he can about them, and try to win their trust and respect. Without that, the journey and his survival are in question. Naming camels isn’t something that nomads would do, but as his relationship with them strengthens, he decides to name them Squeaks and Chewy. They are lucky enough to meet some of the other inhabitants of this seemingly desolate landscape, such as wolves, saiga antelopes and yaks. But will he be lucky enough to catch sight of the most endangered bear on the planet – the Gobi Bear? Spending time with different nomads also gives Gordon time to reflect on the appeal of the traditional nomadic way of life, and his own modern existence. Ultimately, he discovers how camels have evolved in the most unusual ways to survive and prosper in one of the most hostile environments on the planet.

programme.title: Lena Zavaroni: The Forgotten Child Star
programme.desc: Lena Zavaroni was a child superstar, barnstorming the charts, sharing the stage with Sinatra and performing for the US president, all before her 11th birthday. But her light was dimmed too soon by a battle with anorexia. Told from the perspective of her 84-year-old father, Victor, this poignant story reflects on parental regret as he seeks peace with his daughter's untimely fate.

programme.desc: The tale of one of the largest dinosaurs ever to walk the earth, a colossal, long-necked Lusotitan. Living 150 million years ago on an island known as the Iberian Mesta, now in Portugal, this 25-metre-long titan dwarfs every other dinosaur in the region. Yet its intimidating size is only part of the story. The ultimate goal of the male of the species is to win over a female and secure his legacy. It’s a quest that sees him embark on an epic journey as he risks his life for love.

programme.title: Early Man
programme.desc: Young Dug’s sheltered life with his Stone Age tribe is shattered by bronze-mining invaders led by greedy Lord Nooth. To win his home back, desperate Dug gambles on challenging these more sophisticated folk in a contest they love, but he only knows from rock paintings: football. Animated comedy fun from Aardman.

programme.title: Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Shaun escapes through a ‘portal’ inside Shirley’s wool to flee an annoying Bitzer, only to emerge into a chaotic version of the farm without him. Desperate to escape, he repeatedly jumps back inside Shirley, emerging somewhere worse each time!

programme.title: Wallace & Gromit: A Matter of Loaf and Death
programme.desc: Wallace and Gromit have opened a new bakery - Top Bun - and business is booming, not least because a deadly Cereal Killer has murdered all the other bakers in town. Gromit is worried that they may be the next victims, but Wallace does not care, as he has fallen head over heels in love with Piella Bakewell, former star of the Bake-O-Lite bread commercials. So Gromit is left to run things on his own, when he would much rather be getting better acquainted with Piella's lovely pet poodle Fluffles. But then Gromit makes a shocking discovery which points to the killer's true identity. Can he save his master from becoming the next baker to be butchered? And does Fluffles know more than she is saying? It all adds up to a classic 'who-doughnut' mystery, as four-time Academy Award-winning director Nick Park creates a hilarious new masterpiece in the tradition of 'master of suspense' Alfred Hitchcock. Featuring the voices of Peter Sallis (Wallace) and Sally Lindsay (Piella Bakewell).

programme.title: Ludwig
programme.desc: Puzzle setter John ‘Ludwig’ Taylor’s life of solitude is upended when his identical twin, DCI James Taylor, disappears. Drafted in by his sister-in-law Lucy, John reluctantly assumes his brother's identity as a detective in the Cambridge Police Authority in order to find clues to his brother’s whereabouts. John is tasked with infiltrating the major investigations team, gathering information and solving a completely unconnected murder, all whilst remaining in character as his brother. A difficult ask for anyone, let alone a reclusive puzzle-setting genius who rarely leaves the house. Can this master of all things cryptic crack his biggest puzzle yet?

programme.title: Amandaland
programme.desc: Following her divorce, Amanda finds herself downsizing from Chiswick to So-ha (South Harlesden). Amanda rekindles her friendship with Anne, her ex-bff from the old primary school gates. Amanda’s children, Georgie and Manus, have recently moved to the same local high school as Anne’s son Darius. Amanda is delighted when Georgie befriends Morten, the daughter of celebrity chef Della Fry, the owner of trendy local eatery SHIN. Realising her way in is through the local football club, Amanda signs the kids up to Hounslow Eagle FC, despite having zero interest in soccer. Meanwhile, Anne organises welcome drinks to introduce Amanda to the ‘Anne Gang’ the same night as Georgie’s invited to Morten’s house party at Della and her wife Fi’s house. Amanda is torn. Does she go and 'sink some fizz' with Anne, or does she capitalise on the opportunity to take a dip in Della and Fi’s hot tub? While all this is going on, Amanda’s mother Felicity offers to babysit Manus (mainly to avoid her PA/carer Joy), and Amanda continues to contest the parking space outside her flat with her neighbour and fellow school parent Mal. In turn, Mal navigates the world of co-parenting with his son’s step-dad, JJ.

programme.title: Amandaland
programme.desc: Things are looking up for Amanda when she’s approached for a photoshoot of her new ‘minimalist’ home. It's for a local estate agent’s free paper, but it’s still a photoshoot! However, her attempts at a 'simpleton lifestyle', as she calls it, are foiled when Felicity insists Amanda finally empty all the stuff from her mother’s garage. Luckily, it’s the football club’s annual car boot, so Anne persuades Amanda to take a stall and part with some of her ‘curated pieces’ - all her old stuff from her massive Chiswick House - for a good cause. Also, Della is doing the barbecue, so it’s a great opportunity for more social climbing. Meanwhile, Felicity attends her old friend Bunny’s funeral, and Mal struggles with his ex-wife’s clear out of all their keepsakes. Anne becomes obsessed with discovering the identity of her son’s new girlfriend - or boyfriend - and Fi takes up basketry.

programme.title: Amandaland
programme.desc: When Amanda’s Tesla is towed away due to another failed repayment, Amanda is forced to admit that maybe her social media brand Senuous isn’t quite the money spinner she had hoped for. She decides to collaborate ('co-lab') with a local kitchen shop – Kichen’s Kitchens and Bathrooms – in the hope of making a quick buck, though she is keen not to make this public knowledge. All this coincides with parents' evening, where Amanda is told that her daughter Georgie needs to focus more. Unfortunately, her new work schedule means she is unable to oversee Georgie’s homework, so she calls on a favour from Anne to help tutor her. Anne is thrilled at the idea of shaping young minds - she has always wanted to be a teacher herself - but it’s not as easy as it seems. Meanwhile, Mal struggles with helping his own son with his maths coursework, and Della and Fi launch their sister restaurant, Double Shin.

programme.desc: This film looks at the rivalry between Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, which transcended clubs, countries and competitions for over a decade, to become the defining story of modern football.

programme.title: Death Valley
programme.desc: A sudden death at the funeral of a rugby club groundsman leads John and Janie to suspect everyone in the club. With Janie’s big move looming, John considers life without her.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Lee Burkhill and Joe Swift are in Hampshire to help Jan and Darren transform their shaded, north-facing plot into a Sorrento-meets-Lake District retreat. Inspired by holidays to Italy and the Lake District, where Darren proposed to Jan, the couple want a garden filled with memories, texture and tranquillity. They dream of gravel paths, olive-toned Mediterranean planting and central trees for shade, paired with ferns and shade-loving species that nod to the Lake District. Accessibility is vital: Jan, living with a slow-growing form of skin cancer, longs for a sheltered, sun-free space to relax and enjoy sensory plants. Wildlife is also at the heart of their vision, with a hedgehog house on the wish list. Can the team deliver a family-friendly, wildlife haven that blends Italian warmth with Cumbrian charm – all on a £5,000 budget?

programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc: A stop-and-search uncovers cannabis, CCTV supports a mall assault inquiry, and officers track risky teen riders as a long-serving officer ends her shift with major career news.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: Hidden behind two famous gardens lie the legacies of two extraordinary designers: garden designer Gertrude Jekyll at Munstead Wood, one of the National Trust's newest properties, and flamboyant set designer Oliver Messel at Nymans, which overlooks the Sussex Weald. Together, they feature secret laboratories and historic seedlings, topiary cats and exquisite portraits.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson
programme.desc: Nick Robinson in conversation with people who influence our political thinking.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: The quiz show where players must avoid Impossible answers to stay in the competition. 21 people start today’s show but how many of them will survive to face the £10,000 question? Game show presented by Rick Edwards in which players score points by answering questions correctly while avoiding the impossible answers.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents the first semi-final of the classic quiz where contenders return to the black chair under the glare of the spotlight and the ticking clock to win a place in the grand final. The specialist subjects are Oscar-winning performances of the 1990s, the life and death of stars, Peep Show and The Great Escape.

programme.title: Chris and Meg's Wild Summer
programme.desc: Chris Packham and stepdaughter Megan McCubbin continue their wildlife-watching road trip round Britain, this time exploring the rugged Cairngorms in Scotland. Chris and Meg explore the ancient Caledonian woodlands of Abernethy National Nature Reserve, where Chris is on a mission to show Meg a very rare flower. Deep in the forest they eventually find what Chris was looking for: the twinflower. The next day, Chris and Meg head to the tranquillity of Loch Insh in search of one of our most impressive birds of prey – the osprey. Once hunted to extinction in Scotland, these fish-eating raptors are now successfully breeding in the highlands again. Their next stop is another loch – the beautiful Loch an Eilein with its island castle - where Chris recounts to Meg a story from his youth, complete with his diary entry from the time. Rounding off their second day, the pair head to a wildlife hide in Strathspey in the hope of spotting an elusive mammal - the pine marten - but they find badgers instead. Lastly, Meg has something a bit more energetic planned: a deer-watching trip up a Cairngorms mountain.

programme.title: Chris and Meg's Wild Summer
programme.desc: Chris Packham and Meg McCubbin’s wildlife-watching road trip draws to a close with golden eagles on Harris, Risso’s dolphins off the Lewis coast and a few surprises for the pair.

programme.title: Britain and the Sea
programme.desc: Having examined the sea as a source of exploration, defence and trade, David Dimbleby explores how it emerged as a source of pleasure, Punch and Judy and sand sculpture. Starting at Gorleston-on-Sea, David explores the creation of a seaside holiday culture that remains uniquely British to this day. Sailing down the Suffolk and Essex coasts and into the Thames, David also shows how the sea became an irresistible subject for our most celebrated artists and architects, before finally docking in the very heart of British maritime power - Greenwich.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: This stunningly beautiful film reveals the unique wildlife of the Scottish Highlands, seen through the eyes of film-maker Fergus Beeley. Based for a year at Loch Maree and the surrounding hills in Scotland's far north west, Beeley presents his personal view of the shy animals whose lives are ruled by the rains. He follows the fortunes of rare black-throated divers and white-tailed sea eagles, which both breed there, while capturing the red deer and salmon whose lives also revolve around the loch. With an evocative score provided by local musician Phil Cunningham, this enchanting film captures the magic of a very special place.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from Wrest Park, a 19th-century French-style chateau in the Bedfordshire countryside. Antiques experts Christina Trevanion and David Harper take a look at the antiques and collectables brought in by the public. Paul also heads to Hemel Hempstead to find out how Frogmore Paper Mill became the birthplace of paper's industrial revolution by bringing paper to the masses.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Harry Aikines-Aryeetey, Ania Magliano, Joe Swash and Jasmine Takhar take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Aboard the Golden Pass Express, Michael Portillo wends his way in style down steep mountainsides from Interlaken to the Swiss Riviera. In Lausanne, he contends with a knife-wielding robotic arm at a renowned centre of science and technology. Michael is impressed by the robot’s skills in the kitchen and witnesses a groundbreaking prosthetic that allows amputees to feel heat and cold. At a family-run dairy and Gruyere cheese producer, Michael marvels at the Gruyere wheels floating in their salt baths before tucking into a fondue.

programme.title: Cricket: Today at the Test
programme.desc: Day 2 highlights from the third Test match between England and New Zealand.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: At Longmeadow, Monty is in full summer mode - revamping and refreshing borders to keep the garden looking its best right through the season. He turns his attention to the cucurbit family, planting melons and squash, shares a simple trick to extend the flowering of hardy geraniums, and sows perennial seeds for spectacular colour next year. Arit Anderson heads to south east London to discover the striking transformation of a garden that was once a derelict space into a bold, contemporary community garden powered by creativity, collaboration and clever planting. Rachel de Thame explores how self-seeding plants can be carefully choreographed to create a beautifully natural, flowing design. There’s a passionate grower dedicated to the National Collection of penstemons, and in the Yorkshire Dales, a florist and lifelong gardener shares a deeply personal story of resilience - finding strength, purpose and renewed creativity through rebuilding a garden after a life-changing diagnosis.

programme.title: My Tiger Family
programme.desc: An epic 50-year story of an Indian tiger clan and its five most charismatic and powerful tigresses, who have revealed more about the lives of tigers than anyone thought possible. Their home is Ranthambhore, a magical landscape in Rajasthan dominated by a huge, ancient fort and three crocodile-filled lakes teeming with tiger prey. One passionate man, Valmik Thapar, has dedicated his life to following the big cats, witnessing the most remarkable tiger behaviour ever seen and filmed.

programme.title: Inside No. 9
programme.desc: Felix is pretty certain his wife is up to something with her boss Dmitri, so he decides to hire some help to prove things one way or the other. When professional lip-reader Iris arrives with her powerful binoculars, the couple stake out a hotel bedroom and start to gather their evidence.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Lucy Hockings.

programme.title: Psycho
programme.desc: Absconding with $40,000 of her employer's money, Marion Crane sets off to join her lover Sam Loomis. After a tiring journey through the rain, she stops at a lonely motel run by Norman Bates, an intense young man living in the remote mansion with his domineering mother.

programme.title: Dark Waters
programme.desc: Past ties drag corporate lawyer Rob into conflict with a company blamed for polluting a local stream. But as the case goes on, Rob discovers that the scope of the actual damage is staggeringly vast.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers

programme.title: Cricket: Today at the Test

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Lucy Hockings.

programme.title: Psycho
programme.desc: Absconding with $40,000 of her employer's money, Marion Crane sets off to join her lover Sam Loomis. After a tiring journey through the rain, she stops at a lonely motel run by Norman Bates, an intense young man living in the remote mansion with his domineering mother.

programme.title: Dark Waters
programme.desc: Past ties drag corporate lawyer Rob into conflict with a company blamed for polluting a local stream. But as the case goes on, Rob discovers that the scope of the actual damage is staggeringly vast.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Izzie and JJ help Michael and Clara clear their busy home and revive forgotten gems to sell at auction, but will they raise enough to give Michael’s parents a day out to remember?

programme.title: Two Weeks in August
programme.desc: The group are trapped indoors by a heatwave, and Jess decides to get her family on the next boat home. Tensions mount as the power shorts, the stolen money resurfaces and unwanted visitors threaten to destroy Zoe’s chance at happiness with Solomon. Can she escape what the Fates seem to have in store for her? Nat and Jacob have some making up to do, but as the temperature soars, they too are pushed to breaking point. This isn’t going to end well.

programme.title: Rivals: Messi v Ronaldo
programme.desc: This film looks at the rivalry between Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, which transcended clubs, countries and competitions for over a decade, to become the defining story of modern football.

programme.title: Death Valley
programme.desc: A sudden death at the funeral of a rugby club groundsman leads John and Janie to suspect everyone in the club. With Janie’s big move looming, John considers life without her.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Lee Burkhill and Joe Swift are in Hampshire to help Jan and Darren transform their shaded, north-facing plot into a Sorrento-meets-Lake District retreat. Inspired by holidays to Italy and the Lake District, where Darren proposed to Jan, the couple want a garden filled with memories, texture and tranquillity. They dream of gravel paths, olive-toned Mediterranean planting and central trees for shade, paired with ferns and shade-loving species that nod to the Lake District. Accessibility is vital: Jan, living with a slow-growing form of skin cancer, longs for a sheltered, sun-free space to relax and enjoy sensory plants. Wildlife is also at the heart of their vision, with a hedgehog house on the wish list. Can the team deliver a family-friendly, wildlife haven that blends Italian warmth with Cumbrian charm – all on a £5,000 budget?

programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc: A stop-and-search uncovers cannabis, CCTV supports a mall assault inquiry, and officers track risky teen riders as a long-serving officer ends her shift with major career news.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: Hidden behind two famous gardens lie the legacies of two extraordinary designers: garden designer Gertrude Jekyll at Munstead Wood, one of the National Trust's newest properties, and flamboyant set designer Oliver Messel at Nymans, which overlooks the Sussex Weald. Together, they feature secret laboratories and historic seedlings, topiary cats and exquisite portraits.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson
programme.desc: Nick Robinson in conversation with people who influence our political thinking.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: The quiz show where players must avoid Impossible answers to stay in the competition. 21 people start today’s show but how many of them will survive to face the £10,000 question? Game show presented by Rick Edwards in which players score points by answering questions correctly while avoiding the impossible answers.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents the first semi-final of the classic quiz where contenders return to the black chair under the glare of the spotlight and the ticking clock to win a place in the grand final. The specialist subjects are Oscar-winning performances of the 1990s, the life and death of stars, Peep Show and The Great Escape.

programme.title: Chris and Meg's Wild Summer
programme.desc: Chris Packham and stepdaughter Megan McCubbin continue their wildlife-watching road trip round Britain, this time exploring the rugged Cairngorms in Scotland. Chris and Meg explore the ancient Caledonian woodlands of Abernethy National Nature Reserve, where Chris is on a mission to show Meg a very rare flower. Deep in the forest they eventually find what Chris was looking for: the twinflower. The next day, Chris and Meg head to the tranquillity of Loch Insh in search of one of our most impressive birds of prey – the osprey. Once hunted to extinction in Scotland, these fish-eating raptors are now successfully breeding in the highlands again. Their next stop is another loch – the beautiful Loch an Eilein with its island castle - where Chris recounts to Meg a story from his youth, complete with his diary entry from the time. Rounding off their second day, the pair head to a wildlife hide in Strathspey in the hope of spotting an elusive mammal - the pine marten - but they find badgers instead. Lastly, Meg has something a bit more energetic planned: a deer-watching trip up a Cairngorms mountain.

programme.title: Chris and Meg's Wild Summer
programme.desc: Chris Packham and Meg McCubbin’s wildlife-watching road trip draws to a close with golden eagles on Harris, Risso’s dolphins off the Lewis coast and a few surprises for the pair.

programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Harry Aikines-Aryeetey, Ania Magliano, Joe Swash and Jasmine Takhar take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Aboard the Golden Pass Express, Michael Portillo wends his way in style down steep mountainsides from Interlaken to the Swiss Riviera. In Lausanne, he contends with a knife-wielding robotic arm at a renowned centre of science and technology. Michael is impressed by the robot’s skills in the kitchen and witnesses a groundbreaking prosthetic that allows amputees to feel heat and cold. At a family-run dairy and Gruyere cheese producer, Michael marvels at the Gruyere wheels floating in their salt baths before tucking into a fondue.

programme.title: Cricket: Today at the Test
programme.desc: Day 2 highlights from the third Test match between England and New Zealand.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: At Longmeadow, Monty is in full summer mode - revamping and refreshing borders to keep the garden looking its best right through the season. He turns his attention to the cucurbit family, planting melons and squash, shares a simple trick to extend the flowering of hardy geraniums, and sows perennial seeds for spectacular colour next year. Arit Anderson heads to south east London to discover the striking transformation of a garden that was once a derelict space into a bold, contemporary community garden powered by creativity, collaboration and clever planting. Rachel de Thame explores how self-seeding plants can be carefully choreographed to create a beautifully natural, flowing design. There’s a passionate grower dedicated to the National Collection of penstemons, and in the Yorkshire Dales, a florist and lifelong gardener shares a deeply personal story of resilience - finding strength, purpose and renewed creativity through rebuilding a garden after a life-changing diagnosis.

programme.title: My Tiger Family
programme.desc: An epic 50-year story of an Indian tiger clan and its five most charismatic and powerful tigresses, who have revealed more about the lives of tigers than anyone thought possible. Their home is Ranthambhore, a magical landscape in Rajasthan dominated by a huge, ancient fort and three crocodile-filled lakes teeming with tiger prey. One passionate man, Valmik Thapar, has dedicated his life to following the big cats, witnessing the most remarkable tiger behaviour ever seen and filmed.

programme.title: Inside No. 9
programme.desc: Felix is pretty certain his wife is up to something with her boss Dmitri, so he decides to hire some help to prove things one way or the other. programme.title: Newsnight

programme.title: Psycho
programme.desc: Absconding with $40,000 of her employer's money, Marion Crane sets off to join her lover Sam Loomis. After a tiring journey through the rain, she stops at a lonely motel run by Norman Bates, an intense young man living in the remote mansion with his domineering mother.

programme.title: Dark Waters
programme.desc: Past ties drag corporate lawyer Rob into conflict with a company blamed for polluting a local stream. But as the case goes on, Rob discovers that the scope of the actual damage is staggeringly vast.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Izzie and JJ help Michael and Clara clear their busy home and revive forgotten gems to sell at auction, but will they raise enough to give Michael’s parents a day out to remember?

programme.title: Two Weeks in August
programme.desc: The group are trapped indoors by a heatwave, and Jess decides to get her family on the next boat home. Tensions mount as the power shorts, the stolen money resurfaces and unwanted visitors threaten to destroy Zoe’s chance at happiness with Solomon. Can she escape what the Fates seem to have in store for her? Nat and Jacob have some making up to do, but as the temperature soars, they too are pushed to breaking point. This isn’t going to end well.

programme.title: Rivals: Messi v Ronaldo
programme.desc: This film looks at the rivalry between Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, which transcended clubs, countries and competitions for over a decade, to become the defining story of modern football.

programme.title: Death Valley
programme.desc: A sudden death at the funeral of a rugby club groundsman leads John and Janie to suspect everyone in the club. With Janie’s big move looming, John considers life without her.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Lee Burkhill and Joe Swift are in Hampshire to help Jan and Darren transform their shaded, north-facing plot into a Sorrento-meets-Lake District retreat. Inspired by holidays to Italy and the Lake District, where Darren proposed to Jan, the couple want a garden filled with memories, texture and tranquillity. They dream of gravel paths, olive-toned Mediterranean planting and central trees for shade, paired with ferns and shade-loving species that nod to the Lake District. Accessibility is vital: Jan, living with a slow-growing form of skin cancer, longs for a sheltered, sun-free space to relax and enjoy sensory plants. Wildlife is also at the heart of their vision, with a hedgehog house on the wish list. Can the team deliver a family-friendly, wildlife haven that blends Italian warmth with Cumbrian charm – all on a £5,000 budget?

programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc: A stop-and-search uncovers cannabis, CCTV supports a mall assault inquiry, and officers track risky teen riders as a long-serving officer ends her shift with major career news.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: Hidden behind two famous gardens lie the legacies of two extraordinary designers: garden designer Gertrude Jekyll at Munstead Wood, one of the National Trust's newest properties, and flamboyant set designer Oliver Messel at Nymans, which overlooks the Sussex Weald. Together, they feature secret laboratories and historic seedlings, topiary cats and exquisite portraits.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson
programme.desc: Nick Robinson in conversation with people who influence our political thinking.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: The quiz show where players must avoid Impossible answers to stay in the competition. 21 people start today’s show but how many of them will survive to face the £10,000 question? Game show presented by Rick Edwards in which players score points by answering questions correctly while avoiding the impossible answers.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents the first semi-final of the classic quiz where contenders return to the black chair under the glare of the spotlight and the ticking clock to win a place in the grand final. The specialist subjects are Oscar-winning performances of the 1990s, the life and death of stars, Peep Show and The Great Escape.

programme.title: Chris and Meg's Wild Summer
programme.desc: Chris Packham and stepdaughter Megan McCubbin continue their wildlife-watching road trip round Britain, this time exploring the rugged Cairngorms in Scotland. Chris and Meg explore the ancient Caledonian woodlands of Abernethy National Nature Reserve, where Chris is on a mission to show Meg a very rare flower. Deep in the forest they eventually find what Chris was looking for: the twinflower. The next day, Chris and Meg head to the tranquillity of Loch Insh in search of one of our most impressive birds of prey – the osprey. Once hunted to extinction in Scotland, these fish-eating raptors are now successfully breeding in the highlands again. Their next stop is another loch – the beautiful Loch an Eilein with its island castle - where Chris recounts to Meg a story from his youth, complete with his diary entry from the time. Rounding off their second day, the pair head to a wildlife hide in Strathspey in the hope of spotting an elusive mammal - the pine marten - but they find badgers instead. Lastly, Meg has something a bit more energetic planned: a deer-watching trip up a Cairngorms mountain.

programme.title: Chris and Meg's Wild Summer
programme.desc: Chris Packham and Meg McCubbin’s wildlife-watching road trip draws to a close with golden eagles on Harris, Risso’s dolphins off the Lewis coast and a few surprises for the pair.

programme.title: Britain and the Sea
programme.desc: Having examined the sea as a source of exploration, defence and trade, David Dimbleby explores how it emerged as a source of pleasure, Punch and Judy and sand sculpture. Starting at Gorleston-on-Sea, David explores the creation of a seaside holiday culture that remains uniquely British to this day. Sailing down the Suffolk and Essex coasts and into the Thames, David also shows how the sea became an irresistible subject for our most celebrated artists and architects, before finally docking in the very heart of British maritime power - Greenwich.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: This stunningly beautiful film reveals the unique wildlife of the Scottish Highlands, seen through the eyes of film-maker Fergus Beeley. Based for a year at Loch Maree and the surrounding hills in Scotland's far north west, Beeley presents his personal view of the shy animals whose lives are ruled by the rains. He follows the fortunes of rare black-throated divers and white-tailed sea eagles, which both breed there, while capturing the red deer and salmon whose lives also revolve around the loch. With an evocative score provided by local musician Phil Cunningham, this enchanting film captures the magic of a very special place.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from Wrest Park, a 19th-century French-style chateau in the Bedfordshire countryside. Antiques experts Christina Trevanion and David Harper take a look at the antiques and collectables brought in by the public. Paul also heads to Hemel Hempstead to find out how Frogmore Paper Mill became the birthplace of paper's industrial revolution by bringing paper to the masses.

programme.desc: Grasslands cover one-quarter of all land and support the vast gatherings of wildlife, but to survive here animals must endure the most hostile seasonal changes on the planet. From Asia's bizarre-looking saiga antelope to the giant anteaters of Brazil, grassland animals have adapted in extraordinary ways to cope with these extremes. In the flooded Okavango, lions take on formidable buffalo in epic battles, on the savannah, bee-eaters take advantage of elephants to help catch insects and, on the freezing northern tundra, caribou embark on great migrations shadowed by hungry arctic wolves.

Coach Lisa has given the girls a new challenge – not only do they have to perfect their routine, but they also have to choreograph part of it themselves.

By the time they return to the ice lollies, all that's left are the sticks and a plate of lolly goo.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: After a fun waving game with the Tiddlytubbies, the Teletubbies enjoy watching children waving as they set off on a short boat trip. Finally, the Teletubbies wave to the Tiddlytubbies, who are off to sleepybyes.

programme.title: Tee and Mo

programme.title: Colourblocks

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing has broken his arm and is struggling to do his usual activities. Petting Arlo hurts, playing with blocks hurts, and even drinking juice hurts. But when Bing and Sula draw together it doesn't hurt, and so he forgets about his arm and does a big, painful 'hoppity voosh'! Amma gently explains to Bing, Sula and Flop that when she broke her arm, she learnt that sometimes you have to ask for help.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Tao can’t go on with his circus performance, so there are going to be some disappointed fans, unless Bo agrees to do all the acts for him - with some help from Mojo’s tops!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: It's our favourite grumpy twosome, the Old Deers, introducing this episode, with their usual positive attitude about how everything was better in their day. We start with Duggee’s Counting Train, Hatsu the Pottery Poodle is on hand with a beautiful haiku about singing frogs and sleeping monkeys, and Ethel breaks the peace with a loud toot. Frog throws some shapes, then Enid and a mouse turn into Japanese anime for a colourful cartoon chase across the Clubhouse.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee is encouraging the Squirrels to come outside by gesturing through the window. They don’t understand what he’s doing and think it’s funny. When he comes inside, a bit exasperated, he explains that he was miming. They want to know what miming is, and Duggee fondly recalls his days as a young Parisian street performer. The Squirrels are keen to learn how to mime, and Duggee runs them through the basics.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey learns the power of promises when she sees how much Bingo trusts Mum’s word.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Mum remembers when Bluey and Judo were babies and their race to see who would walk first!

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: Tired of being constantly humiliated, the predators devise a plan that will get rid of that pesky Peter Rabbit once and for all, if they can work together long enough to pull it off!

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventure series. Captain Barnacles and his intrepid band of explorers roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. The Octonauts attempt to keep the peace amongst a trio of mudskippers whose home has been flooded.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Learn how much fun counting can be with the Numberblocks - a fun-loving group of numbers who work together to solve problems big and small.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: Meet the Alphablocks! From accident-prone A to sleepy Z, all twenty-six letters are full of fun and ready for adventure.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: When Nugget’s favourite teddy bear gets accidentally washed by Pancake, the Piripenguins try to restore its unique smell by painstakingly recreating Nugget’s happiest memories.

programme.title: Playtime Towers
programme.desc: Bella and Lift visit Patch in the Cloud Kitchen, but he has lost one of his boots - it was stolen by a cheeky crab. This gives him a great idea for a tasty treat - crabby croissant.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: It's music time at the creche, and everyone wants a turn on the drum. Bing gets impatient waiting for his turn, but as he tries to grab the drum from Sula he trips and breaks it. Now nobody can play the drum.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘pasta’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. This episode is all about pasta - yellow, green and even rainbow pasta. We see Dee and a friend make some cheesy pasta, and Ant goes for a ride in a pasta balloon! The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch
programme.desc: Declan accidentally upsets Gus by not properly explaining the rules of a game.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: In a game of hide-and-seek, Kiri pretends to be a flower.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: The Froglets try gardening, but can they grow a beautiful flower before everyone returns?

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are at an ice rink where they watch a young girl practising a routine where she twirls around. The girl leaves the ice, and the Twirlywoos can't resist having a go themselves, but when they get on the ice and try to twirl they find it's trickier than it looks! The Box visits the boat. It has a grass skirt inside which causes the wearer to twirl around. Each one of the Twirlywoos wears the skirt and is twirled around by it. It then lands on Toodloo who performs a twirling routine, twirling faster and faster. Toodloo looks like a spinning top and careers around the boat out of control - past Peekaboo, who gets spun around! Toodloo twirls around very quickly and is lifted up off the ground and out of the top of the boat! The grass skirt flies off and Toodloo drops back down, landing with the other Twirlywoos.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Today, Justin and his friend go to the dentist for a check-up. Meanwhile, Mr Tumble pretends to be a dentist for his toy patients.

programme.title: My Petsaurus
programme.desc: When Chloe's cuddly toy, Baby Topsy, goes missing, it's a race against time to find him before bedtime.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Preschool series. Laa-Laa and Po play a game of hide-and-seek. They both take turns at hiding. Tinky Winky and Dipsy are hiding too and Laa-Laa and Po find them together.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Nigel and Baby Bear welcome babies Theo, Dionne, Francis, Oliver, Minnie and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Parents, carers and their little ones at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! Nigel’s got some socks, a bib and a wooly hat inside his bag. All the parents and babies have different dressing-themed toys and objects too, which are explored through play, songs and a story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to hide safe, baby-appropriate clothes or dressing-up toys inside a fabric bag or pillowcase, to explore with their baby. Some viewers show how they’ve been getting dressed at home too. The fun song We All Like Getting Dressed features, as does a story about Baby Bear dressing up in different outfits. The Action Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: In Tall Trees Forest, Lisa and the children play soldier skittles, learn signs for men, up and down, then sing and sign The Grand Old Duke of York.

programme.title: What’s in Your Plant Pot?
programme.desc: Food stylist Rob introduces the Fact Pack to edible flowers and explains how they can be used to make food look and taste exciting.

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: Bahati the zebra has an itch she just can’t scratch, so her friends try to help. Hamza discovers wild buffalo and visits some thirsty elephants.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Split has an itch but no scratching stick. Ginger and the Pea-Rexes get creative to help.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey, Bingo and Mum are enjoying playing Keepy Uppy around the house with their last balloon, when Dad joins in and the game becomes the ultimate test of skill.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Join Duggee, a big, lovable dog, as he runs the Squirrel Club, where children can earn badges for learning new skills. Warm-hearted preschool series about trying new things.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: The Colourblocks attempt to solve a rainbow puzzle with the help of new friends Indigo and Violet. Learn about the seven colours of the rainbow with the Colourblocks.

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures
programme.desc: Freddie finds out all about creatures that live on land and underwater – newts. Chantelle is at a zoo to meet Kira and two very special salamanders while Rory and his son Sandy are at a country park to meet a very special protected newt. Chantelle and Rory’s fact files explain why great crested newts are protected, what kinds of newts live in the UK and where they live. It’s also time to find out why newts are important to our planet. This episode’s Teeny Tiny Task is to make a winter home for newts – a hibernaculum.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Freddie and Mum paint colourful dinosaur eggs and organise a tricky treasure hunt for brother George. Will George use his dino knowledge to find all of the hidden eggs and dinosaurs? Later, the boys pretend to be pirates and go in search of another type of treasure. Aboard their pirate ships, they race across a vast boating lake. But who will make it back to shore first? And will they find the pirates' gold coins?

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Molly brings the flavours of the Caribbean to her home by cooking up a Saint Lucian-themed meal for her friends. She makes a feast of jerk sea bass, spiced potato wedges and a tangy avocado and pineapple salsa. Molly loves cooking and has learnt to make this flavourful feast from her dad, who is originally from St Lucia. Her friends taste some raw spring onions and tell us what they think. Spring onions add lots of flavour to her recipe and Molly hopes that her friends will enjoy the taste of them in her meal. Molly sets up a special table in her garden and hopes that her friends will like it when they see all the effort she has gone to.

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: Today, Maddie is finding out how wearing glasses helps us to see more clearly. She visits an optician to see how an eye test works by having one herself. She reads the charts and shapes on the wall and looks into a special camera that takes a picture of the back of our eyes to make sure they are healthy. Then, Maddie shows us how glasses frames are made by shaping gold wire at a factory. Maddie uses a special microscope camera to show us the ant-sized screws that hold glasses together!

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Meagaidh the Border Collie is a search and rescue dog who works with her owner Tom. Her supernose follows scents and smells like clues, so they can rescue people who need their help. Meagaidh and Tom are visiting a school to show the children how a search and rescue dog works. They demonstrate some of their equipment, including Meagaidh’s special doggy goggles, which she wears to keep the wind and dust out of her eyes when she’s in the helicopter. Tom demonstrates how Meagaidh is lowered from the helicopter all the way down to the ground using a special harness. They also demonstrate a practice rescue mission, playing hide-and-seek with the children to show them how Meagaidh’s supernose can follows scents and smells like clues. But when the school cook goes missing with the children’s cheese sandwiches, Meagaidh has to use her supernose for real. Can she help Tom track down the cook and rescue the children's lunches?

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Steve and Aneeshwar meet some Asian elephants and give them a shower with a giant hose. They see how the elephants use their trunk in lots of different ways and discover more about these very clever animals. Their next animal is the ring-tailed lemur, which they meet face to face and learn what they use their long stripey tails for. Finally, Steve and Aneeshwar find what the wild connection is between these two animals.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: It's Evie and Doug's first playdate together with their friends. They try out their new ball pit, but Waffle can't join in because he's not toilet trained. He finds fun elsewhere.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Bernie needs a new shell. Oona and Silky find him the perfect replacement.

programme.title: Small Potatoes
programme.desc: Animated series about a group of potatoes who sing songs in different genres. The Potatoes celebrate the four seasons and sing a folksy song about the exciting things that come with each one!

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: Sonny can’t fit a rescued old tin bath into his caravan. Can TapTap find an unexpected use for it?

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie is at home waiting for the postman. She’s expecting a letter from Uncle George, everybody’s favourite uncle, but each time she hears a knock at the door, it seems to be someone else! Maybe today’s not the day for George’s letter?

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Happy notices a tiny fruit fly on his apple, and the Squirrels are amazed by how small it is. The fly tells them that there are things even smaller than him, and so Duggee teaches them that some things are so small that you can’t even see them – atoms. Combined, these make molecules, which in turn join to make cells, the fabric that makes up every living thing. The Squirrels discover that things can be wide, long, thin or small, and that these attributes make up all sorts of different sizes. To help understand this, they assign a line-up all the way from a small piece of dust to a huge rocket ship.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Sing along to the Numberblocks counting song with the Numberblocks' favourite friends. Learn to count to ten with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. R loves pretending to be a pirate, so she rustles up a ship and takes her crew on a rolling ride through rough seas and rain. Is it all make-believe or will she lead them to real treasure? This episode introduces the letter R and the words rug, rod, rag, rig and red.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin meets Riley and his mum on the pitch to find out about their favourite hobby, football. Mr Tumble makes Grandad a card to show him he cares, but gets into a sticky mess. There's a penalty shoot out in the spotty surprise. Featuring signs for the words mum, hug and scarf.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: The Teletubbies say 'eh-oh' to each other in turn and then say 'eh-oh' to flowers, while the children in Tummy Tales make a friendship circle out of handprints.

programme.title: Andy's Dinosaur Adventures
programme.desc: Andy travels back 65 million years to North America in the time of Tyrannosaurus rex. His mission is to get a clay imprint of the skin of a T-rex. Since T-rex was one of the largest and fiercest meat eaters on the planet, he has to wait for one to fall asleep, but with adorable T-rex babies to look after, the mother T-rex is anything but tired. Will Andy succeed and make it back to the museum in time?

programme.title: Molly and Mack
programme.desc: Molly examines her shelf of special things at the back of Mack’s Stall. She chooses toy alphabet bricks that spell the word ‘yes’ and remembers the day she got them. Alice is playing ‘The Yes Game’. If you say ‘yes’ you are out, and the children enjoy joining in. The kids decide they want to beat the grown-ups at the game, and soon everyone at the Big Hub is playing. Some grown-ups are better at it than others, and Moira finds herself helping Mrs Juniper with all sorts of odd jobs around the Wobbly Coffee Pot Café in her quest to win the game – much to Mrs Juniper’s amusement. Meanwhile, Molly’s mind is on other things, as she wonders what Alice would say if Dad asked her to marry him. Soon, as ‘The Yes Game’ spreads, she thinks of a very clever way to find out.

programme.desc: CBeebies’ very own motorcycle rider, Grace, shows off three amazing racing machines! Grace speeds round her speed track in a touring car, and then she shows off an amazing Formula E car. Finally, she gets to have a spin in an off-road racing buggy!

A wealthy man tells Poirot that he intends to change his will and leave everything to his ward Violet Wilson, but when he is murdered before he can change the document, the old will is stolen from his solicitor's office. The local doctor soon comes under suspicion, but the cool-headed Poirot avoids jumping to conclusions.

programme.title: Law & Order: UK
programme.desc: The gripping crime drama continues with an episode in which there may be more to a seemingly cut-and-dried case than meets the eye. When call girl Katka Cizek is found dead in a pool of blood in an upmarket apartment, only one of her admirers seems to fit the bill for the culprit. He was with her on the night of her death, he does not have an alibi and he has everything to lose if his secret obsession with her were to be revealed. The evidence against him seems clear, and when the matter comes to trial, crown prosecutor Alesha Phillips is given the reins to lead the cross-examination. But as she looks further into the case, Alesha begins to suspect that someone has reason to frame the accused. As she digs deeper, determined to find the truth, she uncovers a shattering betrayal which proves that there are no winners in this case.

programme.title: Law & Order: UK
programme.desc: The police are called to investigate a horrifying gun attack which has left a nightclub peppered with bullets and two victims bleeding out on the floor. But the shocks do not end there, as the shooters begin a deadly rampage through the streets of London. With the media swarming over the case and a hostage in danger, Ronnie Brooks and Matt Devlin find themselves up against the clock as they desperately hunt down the Bonnie-and-Clyde duo responsible for the bloody massacre. When the violent pair are brought to trial, defence barrister Phyllis Gladstone claims that one of the two suspects was more innocent victim than vicious killer. Was the defendant acting out of fear after being beaten and bullied into submission by her partner-in-crime? Aware that there are two sides to every story, the team are under pressure to ensure that someone is held responsible for a murderous spree which has claimed five lives.
